g.title: D1
g.text: D1: Capitalism is contested and definitionally plural

g.title: M1
g.text: M1: Marx: accumulation depends on wage labor and private control

g.title: I1
g.text: I1: Institutions constitute markets rather than merely constrain them

g.title: P1
g.text: P1: Polanyi: land, labor, and money are fictitious commodities

g.title: H1
g.text: H1: Hayek/Friedman: free markets and property yield efficiency

g.title: X1
g.text: X1: Capitalism exploits labor through surplus extraction

g.title: X2
g.text: X2: Capitalism structurally dominates workers or producers

g.title: X3
g.text: X3: Capitalism commodifies and destabilizes social reproduction/nature

g.title: R1
g.text: R1: Capitalism has endogenous crisis or self-undermining tendencies

g.title: W1
g.text: W1: Weber: capitalist durability is culturally motivated

g.title: S1
g.text: S1: Schumpeter: entrepreneurship drives creative destruction

g.title: WEL1
g.text: WEL1: Markets can raise welfare and benefit the worst off

g.title: EFF1
g.text: EFF1: Markets process dispersed information more effectively than planners

g.title: FRE1
g.text: FRE1: Market exchange is voluntary and protects negative liberty

g.title: POL1
g.text: POL1: Economic freedom disperses political power

g.title: R2
g.text: R2: Welfare-state capitalism cannot secure justice

g.title: K1
g.text: K1: Keynes: investment depends on uncertain expectations and liquidity preference

g.title: N1
g.text: N1: Critiques must establish distinctiveness, causality, systematicity, and perhaps non-contingency
